claim.quote: No evidence for νμ → νs transitions is found and we set a world-leading limit on θ₂₄ for values of Δm²₄₁ ≲ 1 eV².

date.quote: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS

key_value_text.quote: We constrain the mixing parameters θ₂₄ and Δm²₄₁ and set limits on parameters of the four-dimensional Pontecorvo-Maki-Nakagawa-Sakata matrix
key_value_text.value: World-leading upper limit on the θ₂₄ mixing angle for Δm²₄₁ ≲ 1 eV², from a νμ-dominated beam over 1.04 km and 735 km baselines with 10.56×10²⁰ protons on target; no evidence for νμ→νs oscillations

name: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS
notes: experiment_ids lists both experiment:minos and experiment:minos-plus because the analysis uses the combined MINOS/MINOS+ near+far detector data set (1.04 km and 735 km baselines) described in the abstract.

significance.locator: arXiv:1607.01176, abstract (no significance/sigma reported for a null/limit result)
significance.note: An exclusion-limit result: no signal was observed, so no discovery significance is reported.

summary.plain: MINOS looked for its muon neutrinos secretly turning into an undetectable 'sterile' neutrino and found no sign of it, setting the tightest limit at the time on how much that could be happening.
summary.technical: Two-detector search for νμ→νs oscillations over 1.04 km and 735 km baselines using a νμ-dominated beam peaked at 3 GeV (10.56x10^20 POT); no evidence found, yielding a world-leading limit on θ_24 for Δm^2_41 <~ 1 eV^2 under a one-sterile-neutrino model with |U_e4|^2=0.

title: Search for Sterile Neutrinos Mixing with Muon Neutrinos in MINOS
why_it_matters: Sterile neutrinos are a leading candidate explanation for the LSND/MiniBooNE anomalies; MINOS's world-leading limit on muon-neutrino disappearance into a sterile state constrained the parameter space available to explain those anomalies via nu_mu-nu_s mixing.
